newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures close slightly down.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures close slightly down.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures on the Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange (TIFFE) closed slightly lower on Wednesday.
The March contract was hurt by the fall in U.S Treasuries overnight and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) tight money market operation this morning, traders said.
The March contract moved in a range of between 99.11 and 99.05 in the day's session. Volume was 86,022 contracts.
The BOJ injected 700 billion yen into the market, less than the market's fund shortfall of 820 billion yen. "The operation has made it difficult to buy," said a dealer at a trust bank.

Another dealer at a long-term credit bank said some Japanese banks were on the side paying fixed rates in the two- to three-year zone in the swap market and that might have prompted some others' hedge sales in Euroyen futures.

But in the afternoon, the March contract recouped losses at one stage, supported by buy on dips, said a trader at a bank. It was also helped by a fairly remarkable rise in Japanese government bond futures, traders also said.
By the close it had slipped again, but traders said the contract's trend was range trade amid a lack of fresh factors.

In the interbank call market, the majority of key overnight calls are likely to be traded at 0.45 percent, up 0.01 from Tuesday, money traders said. They said the weighted average for the day is expected to be 0.45 percent.

The rate rose as the BOJ conducted a tight money market operation for the second day in a row, traders said. Some banks might not have set aside a good deal of funds in this reserve period as the BOJ operation was neutral until Tuesday. So they might be forced to borrow funds aggressively, they said.
In the open market, certificates of deposit (CDs) rates were steady at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT). A huge amount of about 220 billion yen worth of key three-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent.
About 50 billion yen worth of two-month CDs and about 60 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued, both at 0.52 percent.
